title: Why India Needs a Comprehensive Polar Strategy
author: Abhijeet Bharat
text:
A helicopter carries the Indian flag while passing over India’s Maitri research station in Antarctica, Feb. 2, 2005.
Credit: Indian Ministry of Science and Technology
For generations, India’s strategic policies have been anchored by two geographical features: the Himalayas guarding its northern boundaries and the Indian Ocean protecting its maritime boundaries. However, amid renewed scientific and strategic attention as well as great power competitions, other frontiers –  the Arctic Sea and the Antarctic – are quietly redefining the country’s security, economic, and diplomatic landscape.Against this background, the Parliamentary Standing Committee on External Affairs’ report on “India’s Role and Presence in the Arctic and Antarctic Regions” is more than a routine parliamentary exercise. The committee deemed India’s current approach to the polar region inadequate. It recommended appointing a polar ambassador and creating a dedicated Polar Affairs Desk within the Ministry of External Affairs to strengthen capability and pursue a more proactive diplomatic role in both poles.[...]
